analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. I examined both base-text units and the patch excerpt. The head side shows two additions. (1) Around head lines 956-962, the stop/drain section now documents that with the coordinator connection down, a drain with no unfinished work waits up to 10 s for the session to return and then finishes without a coordinator acknowledgement. It also documents that shutdown waits up to 15 s per model unload, and that a model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit. (2) Around head lines 1028-1043, the status section documents a new 'Configuration change needs a restart to apply' diagnostic. It compares the saved enabled_models against the filter the daemon started with, or the one the last committed switch applied. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the rest of the status text.

Security-relevant observations, all documentation of behaviour I cannot verify from the supplied evidence:
- The acknowledgement-less drain path appears to relate to the logout and stop flow (A-008, TB-011, T-053). The doc says the disconnect already cancelled accepted work and nothing queued can reach the coordinator. The code in ServiceDrain.swift and ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown was not supplied, so I cannot confirm that claim.
- The documented logout order is unchanged: the provider is stopped and its exit confirmed before token revocation, and the lock is held through local deletion. The logout text is in the unchanged context lines (base lines 552-575).
- Leaving a model to process exit after a 15 s unload timeout touches T-028 (residual GPU memory), but process exit is the cleanup path, so no regression is shown.
- The new diagnostic exposes only enabled_models diffs in the local operator status output. It does not touch token, key or prompt data.

No security controls were changed, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated. The integration questions to check are whether the implementation actually matches the documented offline-drain semantics, and whether the offline-drain skip of the acknowledgement could leave a coordinator-side in-flight state that is never released. That second point belongs to platform-owned code and is not evidenced here.
